12.35.title: Speed recovers with a realistic delay
12.35.description: Getting back to full speed from a standstill, walking, crouching or aiming was too quick; ground acceleration now uses the Unreal Engine character default.
changes: Standstill to 95% of run speed: 0.14 s → 0.26 s with a rifle, matching a community estimate fitted to VALORANT movement (0.258 s) and the Unreal Engine character's default maximum acceleration (2048 cm/s², 20.48 m/s²). Operator 0.24 s, knife 0.32 s.
Releasing walk, crouch or aim also eases back to full speed with the same acceleration (rifle to 95%: walk 0.13 s, crouch 0.16 s, aim 0.06 s).
Stopping is unchanged: releasing a key reaches 25% in 0.133 s and stops in 0.192 s, and counter-strafing is unchanged too.
The portable C++ core for the Unreal port was regenerated with the current rules (acceleration and the 12.27 weapon values).
The new behaviour applies only under the new simulation rules (replay simulation 10); earlier replays play with the rules they were recorded with.

12.34.title: Movement physics consistency: knife jump speed, silent landing
12.34.description: After repeated checks of 360 jump scenarios, 208 ground transitions, chained hops and random sessions, the air speed caps that were computed differently now follow one rule, and a crouched jump stood up in the air lands silently.
changes: Knife jump speed: jumping backwards or crouching on the jump with the knife cut speed to 5.94 m/s (on the live 12.22 site every knife jump and hop was cut to 5.67 m/s). Every air speed cap now scales with the weapon's run speed, so the knife keeps its ground speed on any jump.

Silent landing: jumping while already crouched and standing up in the air extends the legs, so you land earlier and softer (about 5.4 m/s) and without a sound. Landings below 6.0 m/s are silent, so drops lower than 0.88 m are quiet too. A normal standing jump on flat ground is still heard.
Aim-down-sights movement (Vandal and Phantom 76%, Operator 72%) matches the official values, and reaches the same speed whatever the order of aiming, or aiming in the air.
Results: under the new rules 0 violations across 360 jump scenarios, ground transitions, weapon switches, chained hops and 64 random sessions, with exact replay playback.
The new behaviour applies only under the new simulation rules (replay simulation 9); earlier replays play with the rules they were recorded with.

12.33.title: Knife grips, aim pose and attack motion redesigned
12.33.description: After researching well-received approaches in other FPS games and real knife grips, the knife was rebuilt with a grip for each design, an aim pose toward the crosshair and attacks that reach it at the moment of the hit.
changes: A grip for each design: the field knife, aether blade and obsidian fang in a forward grip, the tanto in a saber grip with the thumb on the spine, the kunai in a reverse grip with the thumb over the ring, and the karambit in a reverse grip with the index finger through the ring.

Aim pose: the point is canted toward the crosshair and the edge faces the target, without covering the crosshair (checked at 4:3, 16:9 and 21:9). The flat of the blade is visible, so each knife is easy to recognise.
Contact at the moment of the hit: knife hits resolve on the press, so the tip now reaches the crosshair 0.041 s into a slash and 0.074 s into a stab, instead of about 0.1 s late.
Three-swing combo: consecutive slashes cycle through three different directions; a stab or a short pause starts again. Reverse grips hook and drive the stab down from above.
Draw: the karambit spins once round the index finger through its ring and the kunai flips into the reverse grip. The knife is ready at the same time as before.
The arm stays anchored at the lower right during attacks and pumps with the stride while running.
Damage, range, recovery and hit detection are unchanged. Only the view changed, so replays stay compatible.

12.32.title: Jump sound, silent knife walking, precise movement and footstep measurement
12.32.description: Jumps now push off audibly unless you were already crouched about 0.1 s before. Knife walking no longer makes footsteps, and knife jumps keep their speed.
changes: Jump sound: a jump now makes a push-off sound that bots hear like a footstep. If crouch was pressed at least 100 ms before the jump, the jump is silent (92 ms or less is heard), matching a community study of VALORANT replays (94 ms heard, 101-102 ms silent). Landing sounds are unchanged.

Knife walking: walking with the knife (3.24 m/s) was faster than the 2.7 m/s footstep threshold, so it made a footstep every 1.6 m. The threshold now scales with the weapon's run speed (3.375 m/s with the knife), so walking and crouch-walking are silent with every weapon.
Knife jumps: a running knife jump dropped from 6.75 to 5.67 m/s; it now keeps the knife speed.
Footstep gauge: landing and jump sounds now appear in the alert and on the sound map, and the gauge shows the current weapon's footstep threshold.

Movement and footstep measurement: speeds for 5 weapons x 9 movement states, acceleration and stopping times, footstep intervals and gauge recovery were measured and published. Run and aim-down-sights speeds match the official wiki.
The new behaviour applies only under the new simulation rules (replay simulation 8); earlier replays play with the rules they were recorded with.

12.31.title: Bots return, bot-view replays, air crouch and infinite magazine
12.31.description: Eliminated bots now come back on the training maps, and bots react to gunfire. Replays can be watched through a bot's eyes, and crouching mid-air now raises your legs.
changes: Bots return: on the tactical courses, tactical maps and the peeking lab, an eliminated bot comes back after 3 seconds (adjustable from 0.5 to 10 seconds, or off). It returns at its original angle or at another verified spot for that angle, so you cannot memorise a single position.
Bot AI: bots hear gunfire. When you fire within 60 m (40 m for the suppressed Phantom, 70% of that through cover), bots that cannot see you turn their aim towards the sound and stay alert.

Bot-view replays: choose "Bot view" in a replay to watch from a bot's eyes along its actual aim, recoil included. You can pick the bot, its state (holding the angle, checking a sound, alert, tracking, firing and so on) is shown, and your position appears as a translucent silhouette.
Air crouch: crouching during a jump now raises your legs instead of lowering your head. Your feet rise by up to 0.5 m, so you land about 0.06 s later and can reach higher ledges.
Infinite magazine: the ammunition settings gain "Infinite magazine · no reloading". Fire rate and recoil stay the same.

Movement speed by weapon already matches the official values: Vandal, Phantom and Sheriff 5.4 m/s, Operator 5.13 m/s, knife 6.75 m/s. The Sheriff officially runs at rifle speed, so switching between slots 1 and 2 keeps the same speed.
The new behaviour applies only under the new simulation rules (replay simulation 7). Earlier replays still play and verify with the rules they were recorded with.

12.30.title: Map reverb restored on 44.1 kHz audio devices
12.30.description: Map room reverb was missing on computers whose audio device does not run at 48 kHz.
changes: Room responses were prepared only at 48 kHz, which the reverb rejects on devices running at 44.1 kHz or other rates, so those sessions had no reverb. Responses are now rendered at the device's sample rate.

12.29.title: Cloudflare deployment security fix
12.29.description: Fixed a security problem in the deployment settings for the move to Cloudflare. The current site is not affected.
changes: The Cloudflare entry point exposed the GPU streaming grant API, which trusts a user identity header; a forged header could obtain a grant token. The API is only safe behind ChatGPT Sites authentication, so it is not served on Cloudflare.

12.28.title: Review fixes: replay compatibility, reverb volume, knife reach
12.28.description: Three problems found in code review before the site deployment are fixed.
changes: Replays recorded before 12.27 on the renamed courses failed verification; earlier replays are now checked with the course name they were recorded with.
Room reverb stayed audible when the firing, handling, feedback or footstep volume was set to zero; the reverb now follows each volume.
A knife swing could hit a target hidden behind a wall edge; the blade now needs a clear line to the target (earlier replays keep their recorded result).

12.27.title: Original course names and current weapon values
12.27.description: The 13 tactical courses now have original names that describe each layout, and weapon values follow the official wiki and the latest patches.
changes: Course names: Balcony Alleys, Gateway Yards, Three Gardens, Arcade Square, Cold Storage Yard, Coastal Fort, Ring Laboratory, Dome Corridor, Spiral Shrine, Market Crossing, Catwalk Laboratory, Smelter Gate, Ridge Observatory. Saved settings and records carry over.
Reserve ammunition now matches patch 6.11: Vandal 50, Phantom 60 (applies when unlimited reserve is off).
Airborne firing error now matches the official wiki: Vandal and Phantom +10°, Sheriff +7°.

Official patch notes up to 13.10 were reviewed. The recent rifle buff (13.09) targets the Warden, which VALOPRAC does not have; the last Vandal and Phantom change is the 11.08 spray update (0.6 s yaw switch, protected bullets Vandal 6 / Phantom 8), already in place.
Replays recorded with earlier versions keep playing back with the weapon values they were recorded with.

12.26.title: Full audit and quality fixes
12.26.description: The site, gameplay, design, sound and interface were checked end to end, and the confirmed problems are fixed.
changes: The English interface no longer mixes Korean into the knife, graphics settings, benchmark and fundamentals map text.
Knife swings were as loud as a rifle shot; they are now quieter, and drawing the knife matches the other weapons.
Footstep variants on the same floor differed by up to 4 dB and are now matched; gunshot variants are closer in loudness too.
Guide tables on phones can be scrolled with the keyboard, and some guide pages have a corrected page structure.
Fixed the Cloudflare deployment settings, where the security policy blocked the theme script and unknown addresses showed the home screen instead of a 404.
Restored missing validation images and baseline files so the full build verification passes end to end.

12.25.title: Fundamentals training maps
12.25.description: Four original maps each train one aiming fundamental: pre-aiming, checking angles, flicking and micro-adjusting. Targets do not shoot back and only fall to headshots.
changes: Pre-aim Hallway: seven corners each hide an enemy at head height; the HUD shows how far your crosshair was from the head when it first appeared.
Angle Garden: clear seven angles, including a raised deck, while defenders make short shoulder peeks.
Flick Plaza: one target at a time appears at least 35 degrees from your crosshair, sometimes behind you.
Micro Lanes: small heads 25-36 m away strafe a few decimetres either way.

12.24.title: Sound overhaul
12.24.description: Every sound was rebuilt the way shooter audio is layered: gunshots, reloads, hit and kill feedback, footsteps, impacts and the room you hear them in.
changes: Gunshots combine a mechanism click, a sharp crack, a mid body, a deep punch and a tail, in four variations so automatic fire never repeats one sample. Your own shots are in stereo.
Headshots ring with a short metallic dink, body hits thud, and every elimination plays a confirm that rises with consecutive kills.
Reloads are full sequences: magazine out, seat, charging handle; the Sheriff ejects its cases and snaps shut.
Footsteps land heel then toe with the floor's own sound and stay easy to hear; each map has its own room echo, and distant shots sound farther away.

12.23.title: Graphics quality tiers and Ultra performance
12.23.description: Ultra now renders as efficiently as High, quality tiers are laid out like a shooter's video menu, and the game can measure your computer and recommend a tier.
changes: Ultra no longer turns on bloom and ambient occlusion. Every tier draws the scene once straight to the screen; in measurements Ultra's frame time dropped by about 40%.
Settings → Graphics shows a table of what each tier changes. Bloom and ambient occlusion are optional, and ambient occlusion now keeps the image sharp.
Shows which graphics device your browser actually uses and warns when hardware acceleration is off.
Measure on this computer: tries each tier at your screen size and recommends the highest one that keeps up with your monitor.

12.22.title: Graphics options, performance and a knife slot
12.22.description: The main causes of low frame rates at high quality are reduced, graphics options prioritise clarity and frame rate, number keys hold a fixed loadout with a new knife, and switching weapons no longer stops you.
changes: Ultra no longer renders at 1.25× scale, and the rendering resolution never exceeds 4K.
Medium and High use native anti-aliasing only, with no full-screen post-processing. Ambient occlusion and bloom remain on Ultra only.
Ambient occlusion uses half as many samples, and a per-frame crosshair style write that caused hitches is fixed.
Fixed a bug where switching weapons with a number key stopped the player even though a movement key was still held.
1 draws your primary (Vandal, Phantom or Operator, whichever you picked last), 2 the Sheriff and 3 the knife.
The knife slashes with left click and stabs with right click, and you run faster with it out.
Six original knife designs, from real field knives to fantasy blades, can be chosen on the Weapons page.

12.21.title: Training-range materials, lighting and color
12.21.description: One clear key light, a cleaner sky and sharper materials give the range more depth and make targets easier to read.
changes: Targets get a soft rim light along their edges. Choose red, yellow or purple, or turn it off, in Settings → Graphics.
A stronger sun, weaker sky fill and a color-preserving tone mapper remove the hazy, washed-out look.
High quality doubles material resolution, and wall and floor joints are thinner and cleaner.

12.20.title: Interface design refresh
12.20.description: One accent color, a calmer dark theme, and consistent page layout make the training screens easier to read.
changes: Start Training and other primary buttons share the same teal accent.
The dark theme uses neutral graphite surfaces; raised areas are slightly lighter.
Every menu page shares the same spacing and title size, and Korean text no longer breaks inside words.

12.19.title: Bunny-hop trajectory and flight calibration
12.19.description: Public measurements inform jump height, flight time, and diagonal air-strafe acceleration in the VALORANT profile.
changes: Hold W and pair A or D with a matching mouse turn to build a small amount of horizontal speed.
A chained jump starts after actual contact. Running, walking, and crouching use their respective speed limits.
The calibration is based on public jump measurements and a timed route comparison.

12.18.title: Improved VALORANT air steering
12.18.description: Use A or D and turn the mouse to carve tighter airborne turns after a running jump.
changes: Air input turns horizontal velocity smoothly relative to your view.
Time repeated jumps to your landings and alternate left and right turns.
Older replays play back under their recorded physics rules.

12.17.title: Thirteen map training courses
12.17.description: Choose an original course with its own floor plan and terrain in Maps.
changes: Inspect the starting point, route and three defender positions on each course plan.
Gateway Yards includes a one-way transfer gate. Elevated courses include traversable ramps and upper decks.

12.16.title: Korean and English language selection
12.16.description: Choose Korean or English from the Language menu across training, patch notes, the Review Lab, and guides.
changes: Choose English or Korean. Your browser remembers the selected language.
The Review Lab, patch notes, and guides are available in English.
Language changes preserve saved settings, record titles, and custom tags.

12.15.title: Turn your replays into defender movement
12.15.description: Capture movement from your replay, assign it to a defender, and compare your results with a stationary defender in the same setup.
changes: Extract one to four seconds of grounded movement and crouch posture from a recent replay on the same map.
Scrub the path in the floor plan or 3D preview, rotate it in 90-degree steps, or mirror it.
Validate the entire path against walls, floors, ceilings, and map boundaries before using or sharing it.
Start the stationary version from Results and compare angles cleared, deaths, and first-shot headshots.

12.14.title: The Review Lab moves to valoprac.trade
12.14.description: Open the Review Lab directly from training. An exported backup can restore your records and goals from the previous address.
changes: Open the valoprac.trade Review Lab directly from the training history and results screen.
You can import session history, play profiles, and weekly goals as JSON exported from the previous lab.

12.13.title: Connect training records to the Review Lab
12.13.description: Send the session you just completed or export several training records for a single import.
changes: You can go to the Reconstruction Lab to import selected records from your training results and saved individual records.
You can import multiple sessions at once by saving a JSON file for your lab from the Training History screen.

12.12.title: Head-height holds, crouch fights, and defender placement
12.12.description: Practice against defenders who aim at head height, then drag defenders and the starting point to change a scenario.
changes: Original character's headset, chest plate, shin guards and actual hit surfaces
Sit-down engagement with defenders aiming at head height Training new tactical routes
Directly drag the character and starting point on the floor plan/3D Compare the standing/sitting posture of the selected defender
Sit/shoot intervals from recent tactical training or compatible replays are analyzed in the browser and applied to defender movements

12.11.title: Tactical training HUD and start briefing
12.11.description: Review the drill and its settings before starting or after pausing. The HUD displays ammunition, health, and reload status during a fight.
changes: Design applied to the training selection and pause screens to quickly check tasks, maps, weapons, and time
Real-time magazine gauge, ammunition shortage and reload display, actual engagement stamina and time limit display
Connect the changed control keys so that they are reflected in the training guide and adjust the HUD placement on the narrow screen.

12.10.title: Training arena materials and environment design
12.10.description: Each arena has distinct surfaces, cover, and lighting. The editor offers surface patterns with adjustable repeat spacing.
changes: Newly configured stone, plaster, and painted metal, color area at the bottom of walls, and cover borders for each map.
Summary of sky and shadow tones and diagonal floor guidance at the actual training site.
In the scenario editor, you can decorate floors and walls with solid colors, tiles, and industrial panels, and adjust the spacing between repeating patterns.

12.09.title: 3D scenario editing and weapon inspection
12.09.description: Switch between the overhead plan and 3D views to place defenders and inspect a weapon. Convert mouse sensitivity from supported games.
changes: View floor plans, 3D structures, and 3D materials and place defenders by clicking on surfaces
Desert Bronze/Indigo Carbon Finishing and Installed Weapon 3D Inspection
Expression of fine irregularities and roughness of painted metal
Defender appears after crossing the entry line · Applies to continuous engagements and shared codes
CS2·Apex·Overwatch 2·Call of Duty·Destiny 2 Sensitivity Conversion

12.08.title: Saved drills and shot-by-shot review
12.08.description: Save drills to compare attempts under the same conditions. Inspect braking timing and bullet spread for each shot and seek to that moment in the replay.
changes: Save your favorites and recent drills and compare records under the same conditions
Check fire dispersion and braking timing for each shot and move on replays
Sniper picks the door frame and enters the top of the ramp. Defenders appear one after another.
Polar Slate/Cyan Ceramic Weapon Finishes Import Sensitivity and Active Reticle Files

12.07.title: Target proportions and colors
12.07.description: A revised silhouette and outfit colors make the target easier to read at a distance. Hit detection follows the visible glove position in the bent-arm pose.
changes: Model facial contours and hair, adjust leg proportions by increasing waistline and knee position
A turquoise jacket, dark pants and coral armbands differentiate the silhouette by street level.
Match glove judgment to bent elbow posture and maintain model from previous replays

12.06.title: Improved enemy character models and materials
12.06.description: We've redesigned enemy characters' equipment and outfits and made their fabrics, shields, and lenses react differently to light. The shape of the target shown on the screen is also used to determine accuracy.
changes: 3D curved redesign of helmet, visor, chin protector, shoulders, waist, gloves, and combat boots
Different surface reactions and training colors applied to fabric, protective plates, rubber, and lenses
The visible model's triangle is shared for head, torso, and limb shooting decisions.
Reduce vertex and material data size with indexed mesh and maintain existing instancing
Previous replays are played with the target model at the time of recording

12.05.title: Improved wall and cover finishes
12.05.description: Made wall seams and metal cover finishes more visible. Wall finishes were grouped together to reduce throughput, while glass and penetrating practice surfaces retained their individual characteristics.
changes: Joints at the top of the wall, vents, and the metal top and sides of the cover are represented as thin surfaces.
Reduce unnecessary face and shadow calculations by rendering wall finishes at once
Maintains the unique material of the Wall Shot specimen and the transparent expression of glass
Maintain existing cover position, collision and bullet detection

12.04.title: Improved map surface and graphics memory
12.04.description: We tweaked the surface expressions to make concrete, stone, wood, and metal look different. Low and medium graphics settings reduce memory usage by not creating unused textures.
changes: Improved differences in concrete particles, stone grains, wood grains, and metal reflections
Picking lab floor color reflects the actual assigned visual material
Omit creation of unused texture channels at low and medium quality
Save roughness texture as two channels and display with existing shader
Reduce repetitive vertex data on the map while maintaining the location of walls and cover

12.03.title: Improved settings/training tool keyboard navigation
12.03.description: You can move the Settings and Training Tools tabs with the keyboard, and on narrow screens you can scroll the tab list horizontally.
changes: Navigate the wide settings screen with the up and down arrow keys, and narrow screens with the left and right arrow keys.
Apply single-line horizontal scrolling to mobile settings and training tools tabs
Training tool opens a panel and calls up a replay when selected with Enter or Space
Opening batch edits on a tactical path keeps keyboard focus on the edit tab

12.02.title: Improved sensitivity lab navigation and touch operation
12.02.description: You can directly open the desired tab of the Sensitivity Lab via a link. When you refresh the screen or go back, the selected tab is restored, and the touch area has also been expanded.
changes: Provides address directly connected to sensitivity search and aim analysis
Refresh the Sensitivity Lab selection tab and restore it from your browser history.
Move tabs with arrow keys and Home/End and select with Enter or Space
On narrow screens, scroll tabs horizontally and display current tab
Enlarged touch area in training settings and organized 3D preview text

12.01.title: Preview and responsive training screen that runs when needed
12.01.description: Lay out your training setup and map plan to fit the screen width. The 3D preview only runs when opened directly, and the menu and history deletion confirmation window have become easier to use with the keyboard.
changes: Switch training settings and real-world map floor plan placement based on available panel widths
3D preview runs only when selected, graphics resources are released when turned off
Provide menus as links to real addresses Open new tabs and maintain browser navigation
Shortcut to main text and connection of keyboard focus after screen transition · One main text area
Changed deleting history to a confirmation window with Cancel as the default selection Supports Esc and keyboard navigation
Classification of selection states in bright, dark, high contrast, and reduced motion environments
Collapse training ground types and maintain saved settings · No changes to physics, shooting, and replay rules

12.00.title: Physics/material upgrades/training stability checks
12.00.description: We have improved the detection of contact with walls, corners, and stairs, and made the sound and bullet marks different depending on the surface material. Changed physics rules are used for new training, and previous replays are played using the rules at the time of recording.
changes: Maintains 120Hz fixed operation and three movement rules, complements high-speed wall, corner, and ceiling contact and multiple stair movements
22 types of physical surface systems connecting impact surface, field of view, penetration, footsteps, landing, and bullet marks
15 types of self-produced PBR finishes including concrete, wood, metal, rubber, and fabric, and surface patterns based on actual size
Apply shared materials to existing maps, weapons, and targets · Adjust pattern, surface details, and memory for each graphic stage
Improved cost of static collision candidate search and field of view/trajectory queries Verification of decision order and results
Excluding invisible target and defender weapon instances · Batch rendering of cumulative bullet marks
Shader preparation with realistic target and hit effects and low settings for software renderer
New physics rules recorded as Replay Simulation 3 · Existing 10.00 records reorganized with previous rules
Automatic shooting, correct aiming, recoil, footsteps accumulation, AI, sensitivity laboratory, existing training and Korean screen maintenance
Movement correction values and walking landing sounds that require actual measurement of the original work are not changed. Actual device FPS and input delay have not been verified.
When restarting training, previous duplicate determination records of shooting, footsteps, and landings are reset to correct missing sounds.
Unification of existing 10.00 replay loading inspection, supplementation of record limit, search cancellation, and abnormal search value processing
Simultaneous storage/deletion of training records and storage limits are processed in one save operation
Complemented judgment of low ceiling contact and steep inside position restoration of continuous jumps immediately after landing
Removal of bullet marks and impact sounds that indicated the calculated boundaries of overlapping objects as actual surfaces
Block abnormal mouse/time values and supplement application of actual frame limits for software graphics
TypeScript maintained after comparative experiment with WebAssembly at the core of computation. No complete replacement of runtime or engine.

11.00.title: Precision Utility interface redesign
11.00.description: Six menu sections, responsive HUD, and light and dark themes put key training information up front.
changes: Unique screen system centered on warm, bright neutral colors and cyan colors · Basic bright theme
Save light, dark, and system themes separately · Maintain ongoing training and game settings
Six main navigations - Training, Maps, Weapons, Sensitivity Labs, Records and Settings - and a collapsible training list.
A training screen that prioritizes the selected task, number of targets, and starting movements, and an original map selection screen
Concise list of four types of weapons, self-made schematics, sorted values and detailed characteristics to unfold
Eight setting categories: General, Operation, Sensitivity, Aiming Point, Graphics, Sound, Training, and Advanced
Simple HUD at the edges of the battle screen with independent contrasting colors and optional details
View training information while paused · Expand diagnostics and safely return without locking input
Summary of results, sensitivity analysis, charts, and replay controls centered on actual records
Unified Korean screen, easy-to-read letters and numbers, keyboard focus, and reduced motion settings reflected
Maintain existing weapons, recoil, movement, AI, footsteps, judgment and training data

10.00.title: Calibrated mechanics, deterministic replay, and training tools
10.00.description: Review training from first- or third-person views. This release adds a warmup, flash avoidance, and position saving, with calibrated movement and spatial audio.
changes: Takeoff velocity, stance and weapon air-speed budget with continuous reverse steering
Calibrate the VALORANT-profile ballistic jump to a provisional 1.15m target; retain separate CS2 and Classic rules
Reduce first-shot delay only for expert pre-aim situations; preserve beginner and normal reaction profiles
Retain zoom FOV, rifle ADS spread, independent zoom sensitivity and rotation-count diagnostics
Essential jump diagnostics, mode-specific instructions and preserved timing for delayed gunfire
Spatial audio using actual map cover, bot movement footsteps and visible graphics preparation
Ground-contact and static-material batching with optional environment diagnostics; preserve cover and collision
Crosshair outlines, center dot, inner/outer lines, ADS settings, code import and local profiles
Shared deterministic replay of inputs, seed, submitted target poses and integrity checkpoints
Playback, pause, speed, seeking, inspection cameras, highlights and local replay files
One-minute 3D warm-up and camera-turn flash avoidance with immediate same-settings retry
Position save/restore, last takeoff, jump trajectories, shared-replay ghost and third-person review
Five routes in original maps with validated scenario editing, codes and share links
Korean default with optional English; settings and history stay in this browser
Proposed air-speed and jump values remain provisional; walking ratio and silent landing await direct game measurements
Physical GPU performance, input latency, listening effectiveness and native-game parity remain unverified; no online rankings

9.01.title: Air speed, zoom, engagement response, audio, and graphics modifications
9.01.description: The speed when moving in the air and the field of view for each aiming magnification have been corrected. Fixed an issue where defenders who were already aiming would have to wait twice before firing their first shot.
changes: Apply walking, crouching, weapon and ADS wish speeds to VALORANT air acceleration while preserving existing momentum
Use base FOV ÷ zoom consistently for horizontal FOV · 82.4/41.2/20.6° from 103°
Independent rifle and Operator 2.5x/5x sensitivity settings, plus delivered counts per 360°
Remove duplicate first-shot waits for pre-aimed defenders while retaining actual recognition, aim error and weapon recovery
Calibrate Vandal/Phantom ADS first-shot base spread to 0.1575/0.11°
Pin jump, landing and chained-jump diagnostics without scrolling; correct selected-training start labels
Add spatial audio to enemy gunfire and actual bot footsteps; improve original footstep frequency balance
Discard stale gunfire and coalesce delayed sounds per emitter while preserving valid future shot intervals
Guidance for inferred software/integrated graphics and automatic Low quality, preserving manual choices
Prepare shaders, postprocessing and GPU work before starting, with cancellation handling; enable play after the first actual frame
Optimize architectural meshes and material batching in the peeking complex and existing maps while preserving collision and tactical layouts
Separate comparisons from records using the previous aiming projection; native silent jumping remains unmeasured

9.00.title: Dual movement physics and realistic mid-air steering
9.00.description: You can choose how you move in VALORANT and Counter-Strike in the settings. You can practice your sense of changing direction in the air and compare records with the same movement rules.
changes: Choose VALORANT or Counter-Strike movement physics in Settings → Controls · VALORANT by default
Actual air acceleration, momentum and direction changes from A/D/W/S input and view rotation
CS 2-calibrated projection acceleration, ground friction, landing input windows and jump-spam limits, with separate Classic Source rules
Timestamped brief direction inputs, manual jumps and optional wheel jumping ·120 Hz fixed simulation
Validated ramps, stairs, platform edges, ceiling contact and crouched movement
Dedicated material impact sounds and hearing events for actual landings; no airborne walking footsteps
Current physics indicator and optional speed, acceleration, direction, jump and landing diagnostics
Preserve position, vertical momentum, weapon recovery and sensitivity when switching physics; safely reset pending horizontal state
Keep averages and paired comparisons separate for tactical/combat aim records with different movement models; retain existing records
Compare trajectories against the 08.00 baseline and verify determinism across 60/144/240 Hz render schedules
Preserve existing maps, modes, four weapons, AI, footstep accumulation and sensitivity laboratory
Independent calibrations informed by public patch notes; full equivalence to actual VALORANT/CS 2 engines remains unverified

8.00.title: Combat AI, Movement Mechanics, Wall Shot Training
8.00.description: The defender's reaction, aiming, and shooting are implemented step by step, and the difficulty level can be selected. In the training area, you can practice jumping, moving up ramps, and piercing through wooden and metal surfaces.
changes: Separate defender visual detection, reaction, aiming and firing stages, with continuous angular speed and acceleration limits
Actual weapon recoil, spread, ammunition and reloading, delayed imperfect recoil compensation, and distance-based tap/burst/automatic fire
Separate angle learning, ballistic gunfights and exposure limits; beginner, normal, advanced and expert defender settings
Reset magazines, reserves, reloads, bolts, scopes, recoil, input and hearing knowledge after death; prevent duplicate retries
Recover footstep accumulation during actual slowing, prevent silent fast A/D repetition, and retain residual accumulation when walking
Fresh-input jump buffers, chained jumps, airborne momentum and speed limits, with ramps, stairs and low-ceiling practice
Shared weapon hit detection for materials, traversed thickness, incidence angles, penetration budgets, multiple surfaces and attenuated damage
Wood, steel and reinforced-wall penetration training; limited bot wallbangs use prior observations and actual sound without normal line of sight
Material-specific entry/exit impacts, debris and original synthesized impact sounds, with optional penetration/aim developer diagnostics
Landing input timing, speed preservation, bot reaction, aiming and burst analysis, with a restrained Korean interface color hierarchy
Preserve the sensitivity laboratory, four weapons, every peeking zone, settings, statistics and collapsible training menu
